_comment: What everybody knows in the game's time and place (see docs/modding.md, "ai"): small talk the people the player talks
to may use, told them with the facts (a few lines, the rules' ai.talk.loreTold, drawn across the topics they know, the
same all day; the first facts left out when the sheet is too long). Every mod's ai/lore.json goes over the ones before
it key by key: a mod adds a topic, changes one's lines, or takes one out with "lines": [].
lore: one topic per key. lines: one thing known a line, written to the AI. for: the kinds who know it (seller,
salesman, rival, buyer); none is everybody. from, to: the years of the game's calendar it is true in; none, always.
Never put a car's price here: what is for sale is the game's to say.

lines: Kids cruise the main drag on Friday and Saturday nights, from the drive-in to the diner and back again.
The drive-in theater is where everybody takes a date, and half the cars there are for showing off.
Most families have one car; a second one in the driveway means somebody is doing all right.
The gas station attendant fills your tank, wipes the windshield and checks the oil without being asked.
Cops cruise the main drag on weekend nights looking for anybody showing off.
A sleeper is a car that looks slow and isn't.
Three on the tree is a column shifter; four on the floor is what the racers want.
Slicks are drag tires, binders are brakes, a mill is an engine, a rod is a hot rod.
To dig out is to leave hard off the line; to lay rubber is to leave a strip of it on the road.
Dual quads are two four-barrel carburetors; three deuces are three two-barrels.
The speed-part names everybody knows: Edelbrock intakes, Isky and Crane cams, Holley carburetors, Hurst shifters.
Everybody reads Hot Rod and Car Craft for the latest tricks.
Mag wheels like Cragars and Torq-Thrusts are what makes a car look fast standing still.
Big Daddy Don Garlits is the name everybody knows in Top Fuel.
At the strip the Christmas tree counts you down with lights; on the street somebody drops a hand or a flashlight.
Street racers meet on the long straight past the edge of town, where the cops seldom bother to look.
A pink slip race means the winner drives home both cars: nobody runs for slips unless they are sure.
The NHRA started a Pro Stock class this year: door-slammers with big blocks, the hottest thing at the strip.
Most people buy a car on time: so much down and payments every month.
A trade-in is the easiest way to close a deal: the customer's old car is half the down payment.
Customers kick the tires and slam the doors to hear how they shut.
A clean car on the front row sells the whole lot.
The new hot iron is the big-block Chevy 409, the Pontiac 421 and the Ford 406.
Compacts are the new thing: the Falcon, the Corvair, the Valiant.
The VW Beetle is the college kids' car, and there are more of them every year.
The hottest new iron: the Chevelle SS 454, the Hemi 'Cuda and Challenger, the Boss Mustangs, the GTO Judge.
Insurance companies have started charging young drivers through the nose for a muscle car.
Japanese cars like the little Datsun 510 have started turning up, and they run better than anybody expected.
VW Beetles are everywhere; the hippies paint flowers on their buses.
Gas is around thirty cents a gallon.
A burger and a Coke at the drive-in come to well under a dollar.
Minimum wage is about a dollar and a quarter an hour.
Gas is around thirty-six cents a gallon at the pump.
A burger, fries and a shake come to under a dollar.
Minimum wage is a dollar sixty an hour.
On the radio: Dion's 'The Wanderer', Chubby Checker's twist records, the Beach Boys singing about their '409'.
Car radios are AM, and the deejay at night plays what the kids want.
On the radio: Creedence's 'Up Around the Bend', the Guess Who's 'American Woman', Simon and Garfunkel's 'Bridge Over Troubled Water'.
The Jackson 5 are all over the radio with 'ABC'.
The Beatles have broken up; 'Let It Be' was their last single.
The kids with money have eight-track players bolted under the dash.
Kennedy is in the White House.
Everybody still talks about the Russians and the bomb.
Nixon is in the White House.
Apollo 13 came home safe in April, after the whole country followed it on TV.
The war in Vietnam is still on, and every young man knows his number in the draft lottery.
